entities.summary: Rufus Wilmot Griswold was an American anthologist, editor, poet, and critic. Born in Vermont, Griswold left home when he was 15 years old. He worked as a journalist, editor, and critic in Philadelphia, New York City, and elsewhere. He built a strong literary reputation, in part due to his 1842 collection The Poets and Poetry of America. This anthology, the most comprehensive of its time, included what he deemed the best examples of American poetry. He produced revised versions and similar anthologies for the remainder of his life, although many of the poets he promoted have since faded into obscurity.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Griswold's anthology, The Poets and Poetry of America, set a standard for American literary criticism and helped establish Rufus Griswold as a prominent figure in the field. His work had a lasting impact on the development of American literature.
